desc_full: Site:  The site at Development Review Center is generally deemed to be adequate for its current use. This building is part of the San Diego Centre City Concourse development which includes the City Administration Building, the San Diego Concourse, the Concourse Parkade, the Civic Theatre and Exterior Restrooms, and the Development Review Center.  Together, these buildings occupy four urban blocks in downtown San Diego. The Development Review Center is connected to the other building by a basement level tunnel and via an elevated pedestrian walkway to the Concourse Parkade. The roadways are in good condition.  Pedestrian paving is original and in good condition.  The site landscaping is mature and in good condition.  In general the site grading is adequate.  Site lighting and security appears to be in fair condition.  Site lighting is limited to landscape pole fixtures on the north side of the building.  The parking lot does not have lighting except for the street lighting.
desc_site: Substructure:  The foundations are comprised of concrete footings below the concrete structural columns and walls.  The substructure system does not present signs of movement.
desc_substructure: Shell: Floor construction is a structural concrete slab on a structural grid of concrete columns and beams.  The exterior windows are original and in fair condition.  The window seals are in fair condition.  The aluminum frames are coated and exhibit some minor pitting and surface deterioration on the exterior surfaces.  Windows have generally been fixed shut and are non-operational although they originally functioned as casement windows.  Exterior doors are coated aluminum for the main public entries and painted metal doors for the secondary personnel service doors.  The exterior doors are original and are in fair condition.  Exterior walls are concrete and battered with decorative form patterns cast into the concrete on the ground level.  Roof covering for the main building and projected storage roofs is modified bitumen which is a replacement and in fair condition.  The penthouse high roof is also modified bitumen of a later replacement and is in good condition.  There are no gutters or downspouts.
desc_shell: Interior Construction:  Interior partitions are original and in good condition. However, evidence that maintenance is required to assure useful life.  Millwork and cabinets include a combination of original and replacement units and they are in fair condition.  Interior doors include a combination of original and replacement doors which are generally in fair condition.
desc_interior_construction: Interior Finishes: The typical interior wall finish is plaster which is original and in good condition.  Other finishes such as wallpaper are also present.  The primary interior floor finish is carpet which has been replaced and is in poor condition. The original terrazzo flooring remains at the elevator lobbies and public restrooms on each floor.  The original terrazzo remains in good overall condition although the flooring in some of the restrooms is stained and worn.  Most of the ceilings are finished with suspended acoustical tiles which are original and in fair condition.
desc_interior_finishes: Plumbing: Plumbing fixtures are original and in fair condition.  Flush valve water closets and urinals are not of lo-flo design.  Domestic water distribution is provided by copper piping with hot water from the central boiler.  Sanitary sewer piping is comprised of cast iron piping.  There are roof drains and rain water piping which is original.  No issues were reported to the assessment team.
desc_plumbing: Mechanical: The Heating, Ventilation, and Cooling (HVAC) system is predominately a centralized cooling/heating system with energy supply (chilled and hot water) from the central plant located in the 004-Concourse building, which is original and in poor condition. There is also an air cooled chiller in the fire station area which is newer and of apparent good condition.  The heat from this chiller discharges into the fire station garage.
desc_mechanical: Life Safety: There are no fire sprinkler, fire alarm or fire suppression systems in the ground to upper levels of this building.  The fire sprinkler system is limited to the basement only.  The fire station kitchen exhaust hood (level 1) has a fire sprinkler head, no dry chemical fire suppression.  There is a small addressable fire alarm system, limited to the data/IT room in the basement only.  The balance of the building does not have fire alarm.  Fire protection specialties are present.
desc_life_safety: Electrical: Electrical service for the facility is provided by an underground service supplied by on site primary distribution.  The main service distribution is a substation, 12 KV primary, 2000 KVA oil fill transformer and a 277/480 volt secondary distribution of 3000 AMPs.  Electrical service and distribution is original and in fair condition.  Lighting fixtures have been retrofitted with T8 lamps and electronic ballasts in most of the building.  There are still some T12 lamps in the mechanical penthouse and some utility areas.  Fixtures are older and may be original. Branch wiring is original and beyond its expected useful life.
desc_electrical: Accessibility: An abbreviated accessibility survey was not conducted on this facility.
desc_accessibility: Solar Energy Assessment: A solar energy assessment was performed on this facility.  Please refer to the solar energy report section of this report for details regarding solar energy.

desc_full: Site:The site at Facility #000035, Lyons Peak Radio Blockhouse, was constructed in 1961 as a radio communications facility.  The site is generally deemed to be adequate for its current use.  The facility can be accessed from a mountain road, but due to current disputes related to access to the road, the facility must be currently accessed from a helicopter.  The site has a dedicated area for parking with asphalt pavement.  The parking pavement is damaged beyond repair and should be replaced.  The site does not have pedestrian sidewalks.  The site landscaping consists of indigenous vegetation which is in need of maintenance to cut and clear overgrown weeds. Site related plumbing and mechanical systems include a liquid propane gas tank and associated piping.  Site electrical systems include an underground 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire power supply to the building.  There are no site lighting systems associated with the building.  Overall, the facility is in poor condition.
desc_site: Substructure:The building is a one-story concrete masonry unit building and rests on standard foundation and slab on grade.  The building has concrete masonry exterior walls and steel structural framing for the roof structure and deck. There are no signs of settling and/or structural displacement found with the building foundation or building structure and they are in good condition.
desc_substructure: Shell:The building exterior walls are painted concrete masonry unit load bearing walls.  The exterior painted walls and painted wooden trim pieces, such as the fascia, corner guards, vent hoods and HVAC equipment shields, and facility identification number are faded, oxidized, and peeling and need repainting. The exterior doors are metal units and are installed on metal frames. The exterior doors are in good condition, but the painted finish is faded and oxidized and needs repainting. The roof structure is a low sloped metal frame and deck with a coated corrugated metal panel covering.  No deficiencies were found with the roof structure.  However, the roof covering coating is weathered and cracking and should be recoated.
desc_shell: Interior Construction:The building interior walls consist of the interior side of the concrete masonry exterior walls and one interior concrete masonry interior partition wall.  Interior ceiling construction consists of the exposed metal roof framing and deck.  The interior construction is in good condition.
desc_interior_construction: Interior Finishes:The building interior finishes include the painted interior side of the exterior concrete masonry walls and painted interior partition wall.  There are no interior ceiling or floor finishes.  The interior painted walls are discolored, faded, and worn and need repainting.  In addition a section of the interior wall in the southwest corner of the main telecommunication room is spalling and needs to be repaired.
desc_interior_finishes: Conveying This facility does not have any conveying systems. Plumbing:This facility does not have any plumbing systems.
desc_plumbing: Mechanical:Heating and cooling for the building is provided by one roof top mounted package unit rated at around 2 tons that discharges condition air directly into the building. The unit was replaced around 1996 and is in fair condition but has pasted its expected life cycle and replacement is recommended.  Exhaust ventilation is provided by static vents. The wall vents appear to be original equipment and are in good condition.  Air temperature is controlled by a thermostat which is part of a centrally controlled and monitored system and is in good condition.
desc_mechanical: Life Safety:There are no fire protection systems installed in the building but portable fire extinguishers are present. The building does have heat and smoke detectors which are connected to a centrally monitored system and these are in good condition.
desc_life_safety: Electrical:The electrical service is provided to the building from a 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire service. The service is original equipment.  Over time additional sub-panel boards have been added to accommodate additional electrical demands.  The current configuration of the electrical service is inadequate with some of the existing panel boards having circuits exceeding the design capacity of the panel board.  It is recommended the electrical service and panel boards be replaced with equipment with larger circuit capacity.  Branch circuit distribution within the building is 120 Volts for miscellaneous power outlets and lighting and 240 Volts is provided to some equipment. Electrical power is provided to the telecommunications equipment but telecommunications equipment was not part of the assessment. Electrical outlets are standard grounded devices and light switches are standard toggle style and are modern devices and are in good condition.   Lighting fixtures are fluorescent and they have been upgraded to current and modern standards and were found to be in good condition. Emergency power is provided to the building by a 25kW, 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire liquid propane gas generator and associated automatic transfer switch.  Both the generator and automatic transfer switch were replaced in 2008 and are in good condition.  The building does contain intrusion security devices. The security devices are connected to and monitored by a central station and are in good condition.
desc_electrical: Accessibility:This facility was not evaluated for handicapped accessibility.

The parking lots and roadways are not part of the facility.  Pedestrian paving is original and in fair condition.  The site landscaping is mature and in good condition.  In general the site grading is adequate however, there are areas showing signs of erosion at the rear of the building.  Site lighting and security appears to be in fair condition. Substructure:The foundations are comprised of pier and beam.  The substructure system does not present signs of movement.  The entire gymnasium floor is supported by wood post and wood beam construction braced above a sloping grade under the main level.  A lower level built within the wood floor framing contains toilets and showers, which are now abandoned.  The wood posts are supported by concrete piers. Shell:Floor construction is wood framing upon piers with solid wood sheathing subflooring.  The exterior windows are replacements and are in fair condition.  The window seals are in fair condition.  The vinyl frames utilize single glazing.  Window operation is smooth.  Exterior doors are solid core wood for the main entry and the additional personnel service doors.  The exterior doors are replacements and are in poor condition.  Exterior walls are wood framed with solid wood sheathing with stucco with a painted finish on the exterior side, which are replacements and are in fair condition.  Most of the South and East elevations have been repaired with new stucco.   The roof system is wood trusses with wood purlins and solid wood sheathing in good condition.  Roof coverings are modified bitumen, which are replacements and are in good condition.  Downspouts, drains, and gutters are replacements and are in good condition.  Roof coverings and gutters and downspouts were repaired or replaced and are in good condition. Interior Construction:Interior wood framed partitions are replacements and are in fair condition.  Millwork and cabinets are replacements and are in fair condition.  Interior doors are replacements and are in good condition.  A small wood framed mezzanine along the west wall serves as an office space for personnel supervising the gymnasium. Interior Finishes:Wall finishes are painted surfaces, which are replacements and are in fair condition.  The wood framing and wood exterior sheathing is exposed to the interior and painted.  Floor finishes included a combination of maple hardwood in the gym and ceramic tile in the toilets, which are replacements and are in good condition.  The gymnasium floor was refinished in 2013.  Ceiling finishes are painted surfaces and exposed foil insulation and are replacements and in good condition. Plumbing:Plumbing fixtures are a combination of original with some replacements and in fair condition.  Domestic water distribution is provided by copper piping with hot water provided by a central boiler.  Sanitary sewer piping is a combination of cast iron and copper piping.  No issues were reported to the assessment team.  Both the men and women’s locker rooms are no longer used for their designed purpose; all plumbing fixtures in these areas are in poor condition and should be programmed for replacement.  The plumbing fixtures in the restrooms on the gym floor level are replacements and in fair condition.  The majority of the sanitary waste piping has been replaced. Mechanical:The Heating, Ventilation, and Cooling (HVAC) system is predominately a centralized cooling/heating system, which are replacements and in poor condition.  Coils on the air-cooled chiller were in poor condition and the electrical supply to one of the compressors was “locked out” and the other was in the “off” position, the boiler was in poor condition, and the air handling unit and ductwork were in poor condition; all should be programmed for replacement. Life Safety:Fire protection specialties are present.  System components include: hose stations and wet sprinklers.  These sprinklers are provided throughout the building and the hose stations in several locations.  Visually these systems appear to be in poor condition.  The hoses appeared to be in good condition but the sprinkler heads were rusted and appeared to be in poor condition.  The fire protection systems should be programmed for replacement. Electrical:Electrical service for the facility is provided by an underground service supplied by a local utility service.  There are multiple disconnects with an 800 AMP and a 400 AMP main switchboards rated at 277/480 volts.  Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI) receptacles were observed.  Electrical service and distribution a combination of original and replacement components and in fair condition.  Branch lighting and wiring have been upgraded.  This facility’s electrical system is generally in poor condition as the original knob-and-tube wiring is still in place with numerous modifications; recommend a complete system replacement be programmed. Please refer to the solar energy report section of this report for details regarding solar energy.

desc_full: Site:The site at Facility #001471, San Ysidro Radio Blockhouse, was constructed in 1987 as a radio communications facility.  The site is generally deemed to be adequate for its current use.  The facility is accessed from a public mountain road.  The site has a dedicated area for parking with asphalt pavement.  The parking pavement is damaged and weathered in poor condition and should be replaced.  The site has concrete sidewalks for direct access to the building the sidewalks are in overall good condition.  The site landscaping consists of indigenous vegetation and maintenance is needed to cut and clear overgrown weeds.  The facility is encircled by a chain linked fence with both barbed and razor wire across the top.  The chain link fence and barbed/razor wire is in good condition.  Site related plumbing and mechanical systems include a liquid propane gas tank and associated piping.   Site electrical systems include an overhead 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire power supply to the building.  There are no site lighting systems associated with the building.  Overall, the facility is in poor condition.
desc_site: Substructure:The building is a one-story concrete masonry unit building and rests on standard foundation and slab on grade.  The building has concrete masonry exterior walls and steel structural framing for the roof structure and deck. There are no signs of settling and/or structural displacement found with the building foundation or building structure and they are in good condition.
desc_substructure: Shell:The building exterior walls are painted concrete masonry unit load bearing walls.  The exterior painted walls and painted wooden and metal trim pieces, such as the fascia, corner guards, vent hoods and HVAC equipment shields, and facility identification number are faded, oxidized, and peeling and need repainting. The exterior doors are metal units and are installed on metal frames. The exterior doors are in good condition, but the painted finish is faded and oxidized and the doors need repainting. The roof structure is a flat metal frame and deck with a modified bitumen covering.  No deficiencies were found with the roof structure.  However, the roof covering is weathered and worn with much of the top granular surface missing and should be replaced.
desc_shell: Interior Construction:The building interior walls consist of the interior side of the concrete masonry exterior walls and one interior concrete masonry interior partition wall.  Interior ceiling construction consists of painted drywall and exposed metal roof framing and decking.  The interior construction is in good condition.
desc_interior_construction: Interior Finishes:The building interior finishes include the painted interior side of the exterior concrete masonry walls, painted interior partition walls, painted drywall ceilings, painted interior door, and vinyl composite floor tile.  The painted interior finishes of the building are in fair condition but need repainting and a section of the floor tile at the entry door is damaged and needs replacing.

These split systems were replaced around 2011 and are in good condition. Exhaust ventilation is provided by static vents. The vents appear to be original equipment and are in good condition.  Air temperature is controlled by thermostats which are part of a centrally controlled and monitored system and are in good condition.  Life Safety:There are no fire protection systems installed in the building but portable fire extinguishers are present. The building does have heat and smoke detectors which are connected to a centrally monitored system and these are in good condition.

Over time additional sub-panel boards have been added to accommodate additional electrical demands.  The current configuration of the electrical service is inadequate with some of the existing panel boards having circuits exceeding the design capacity of the panel board.  It is recommended the electrical service and panel boards be replaced with equipment with larger circuit capacity.  Branch circuit distribution within the building is 120 Volts for miscellaneous power outlets and lighting and 240 Volts is provided to some equipment. Both the generator and automatic transfer switch appear to be original equipment and are in fair condition, but equipment is past their expected life cycle and should be replaced.  The building does contain intrusion security devices. The security devices are connected to and monitored by a central station and are in good condition.

desc_full: Site:The site at Facility #009977, North City Radio Blockhouse, was constructed in 1992 as a radio communications facility.  The site is generally deemed to be adequate for its current use.  The facility has no dedicated parking areas or roadways, but is accessed using a public mountain road which is not considered part of the facility.  There is no pedestrian paving on the site.  The site landscaping consists of natural indigenous vegetation which is being maintained but maintenance is currently needed to reduce overgrown weeds.  The facility is encircled by a chain linked fence with both barbed and razor wire across the top.  The chain link fence is in good condition, but both the barbed and razor wire are damaged and need to be repaired. Site related plumbing and mechanical systems include a liquid propane gas tank and associated piping. Site electrical systems include an underground 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire power supply to the building and one liquid propane gas fueled emergency generator.  There are no site lighting systems.  Overall, the facility is in fair condition.
desc_site: Substructure:The structure is a prefabricated building and rests on elevated poured-in-place concrete beams which are set on concrete foundation footings.  The building is framed with a steel and wood framed floor and wooden exterior walls and roof structural components. The building is accessed by an elevated concrete ramp. There are no signs of settling and/or structural displacement found with the foundation or building structure and they are in good condition.
desc_substructure: Shell:The exterior walls are prefabricated load bearing wood stud walls and are covered with prefabricated aggregate panels. The exterior walls were found to be in fair condition.  However, moisture damage was found along the interior perimeter flooring and the exterior aggregate wall panels need to be cleaned and sealed throughout with an appropriate weatherproofing material.  Painted metal trim pieces, such as the fascia, corner guards, vent hoods and HVAC equipment shields, and facility identification number are faded, oxidized and peeling and need repainting. The exterior door is a metal unit and is installed on metal frame. The exterior door is in good condition, but the painted finish is faded and oxidized and needs repainting. The roof structure is a flat wood frame and deck with a modified bitumen covering. The roof covering appears to be original. No deficiencies were found with the roof structure.  While there are no visible signs of roof leaks, the twenty-three year old modified bitumen covering is past its expected life cycle and the covering is brittle and weathered and recommended for replacement.
desc_shell: Interior Construction:Interior wall and ceilings are constructed with wood framing which is in good condition.  There are no interior partitions or doors installed in the building.
desc_interior_construction: Interior Finishes:Interior finishes are wood paneling installed over wood studs for both the walls and ceilings and vinyl composite floor tiles.  The wood wall and ceiling panels are in good condition and the floor tile is in overall good condition, however there are sections along the perimeter of the walls that have some moisture damage and need to be cleaned and sealed.
desc_interior_finishes: Conveying This facility does not have any conveying systems. Plumbing:This facility does not have any plumbing systems.
desc_plumbing: Mechanical:Heating and Cooling to the building is provided by two wall mounted package units rated at around 3 tons each that discharge condition air directly into the building. These units were replaced around 2002 and are in fair condition but nearing the end of their expected life cycle. Exhaust ventilation is provided by one wall mounted direct drive exhaust fan and two static wall vents. The exhaust fan and wall vents appear to be original equipment and are in good condition.  Air temperature and exhaust ventilation are controlled by thermostats which are part of a centrally controlled and monitored system and are in good condition.
desc_mechanical: Life Safety:There are no fire protection systems installed in the building but portable fire extinguishers are present. The building does have heat and smoke detectors which are connected to a centrally monitored system and these are in good condition.
desc_life_safety: Electrical:The electrical service is a 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire service. The service is original equipment.  Branch circuit distribution within the building is 120 Volts for miscellaneous power outlets and lighting and 240 Volts is provided to some equipment. Electrical power is provided to the telecommunications equipment but telecommunications equipment was not part of the assessment. Electrical outlets are standard grounded devices and light switches are standard toggle style and are modern devices and are in good condition.   Lighting fixtures are fluorescent and they have been upgraded to current and modern standards and were found to be in good condition.  A 50kW, 120/240 Volt, 1-Phase, 3-Wire liquid propane gas generator with an associated automatic transfer switch is provided for the building for back-up power. The generator and transfer switch appear to be original equipment and are in fair condition but have aged past their expected life cycle. The building does contain intrusion security devices. The security devices are connected to and monitored by a central station and are in fair condition but have aged beyond their expected life cycle.

In general the site grading is adequate.  The domestic water supply is original and in good condition.  The sanitary sewer system is original and in good condition.  The natural gas supply is approximately 22 years old and it is in good condition.  The fire suppression water supply is approximately 3 years old and it is in good condition.  The electrical service is provided by the local utility company and appears to be original and in good condition.  No site lighting or security systems are associated with this facility. Overall, the site at King Chavez High School is in good condition.
desc_site: Substructure:The foundations are comprised of a concrete slab on grade with concrete perimeter walls at the basement level.  The substructure system does not present signs of movement and was found to be in good condition.
desc_substructure: Shell:Floor construction consists of reinforced concrete slabs.  The exterior windows are original and are in fair condition.  The window seals are in fair condition.  The aluminum window frames are coated and utilize single-pane glazing.  Window operation is non-operational because the crank hardware has been removed from all casement windows.  Replacement of the deteriorated UV film on 6 casement windows classroom 301 is recommended.  Exterior doors are aluminum for the main entry and painted metal doors for the additional personnel service doors.  The exterior doors are original and are in fair condition.  Exterior walls are constructed with vertical plaster panels that have a painted finish.  The plaster appears to be original and it is generally in good condition.  Interior sections of the roof parapet walls need repainting. Roof coverings are built up with loose aggregate.  It’s estimated the roof covering was installed around 1988.  The roof presents signs of leaking, ponding, and damaged flashing.  The aggregate is poorly graded causing significant ponding.  Roof drainage is managed with interior piping, receptors, and screens.  The drain piping appears to be in good condition but the receptors and screens are in poor condition.  Replacement of the roof covering, drain receptors, and screens are necessary.
desc_shell: Interior Construction:Interior partitions are replacements installed in 1987 and they are in fair condition.  However, evidence shows that maintenance is required to assure useful life.  Millwork and cabinets are replacements, apparently installed in 1987 with most other interior fittings and finishes.  They are generally in fair condition, but are close to reaching their useable life span and should be replaced within the next three to five years. Interior doors are also replacements (installed in 1987) and are in fair condition.   The interior stairs are constructed of concrete and structurally in good condition.  However the stair finishes, such as the treads, risers, walls, ceilings, and wood rails need refinishing.
desc_interior_construction: Interior Finishes:Wall finishes are paint over gypsum board, which are replacements and are in fair condition.  Due to heavy use the wall finishes should generally be renewed every five years in this facility.  Floor finishes included a combination of carpet and sealed concrete  in the corridors and classrooms which are replacements and are in poor condition.  Floor finishes in utility spaces and restrooms include replacement ceramic tile and resilient flooring as well as original terrazzo.  The tile and terrazzo are in fair condition.  In general, the floor finishes are in overall poor condition and recommended for replacement.  Ceiling finishes include acoustical tiles and painted surfaces, which are replacements and in poor condition and are recommended for replacement.
desc_interior_finishes: Plumbing:Plumbing fixtures are replacements and in fair condition but nearing the end of their service life are recommended for replacement in the next 2 years.  Domestic water distribution is provided by copper piping with hot water provided by a local water heater.  The natural gas fired water heater was replaced in 2007 and is in good condition.  Overall the domestic water distribution system is in good condition. Sanitary sewer piping is comprised of cast iron piping which is in good condition.  Additional sanitary sewer components include 1 duplex lift station located in the basement electrical room.  The lift station appears to be original and functional but it is aged and outdated and recommended for replacement.
desc_plumbing: Mechanical:The Heating, Ventilation, and Cooling (HVAC) system is predominately a zoned cooling/heating system which appears to have been installed around 1993.  Heating and cooling is provided to interior spaces from concealed ceiling mounted fan coil units.  The fan coil units are functional and in fair condition.  However, due to their age refurbishment or replacement of the units in the next 5 years is recommended. Cooling is provided to the fan coil units by a 100 ton air cooled liquid chiller located on the roof.  It’s estimated the chiller was installed around 1993 and the compressors were replaced within the last 5 to 10 years.  The chiller is in fair condition but the condensing coils are deteriorated.  Replacement of the unit is recommended in the next 5 years.  Chilled water is circulated to the fan coil units from 2 chilled water pumps located on the roof adjacent to the chiller.  It’s estimated the pumps were installed around 2003.  The pumps are functional and in fair condition.  Recommend replacing the pumps in the next 5 years.  Heating water is provided to the fan coil units from 1 natural gas fire boilers located in the roof top boiler room.  It is estimated the boiler was installed around 1993.  The boiler is functional and in fair condition but it is an aged, worn, and outdated unit.  Replacement of the boiler will be necessary in the next 3 years.  Heating water is circulated to the fan coil units from 1 heating water pump located in the roof top boiler room.  It’s estimated the pump was installed around 2004.  The pump is in good condition.  Additional heating and cooling components include 1 split air conditioning system serving the 3rd floor electric room.  It’s estimated the split system was installed around 1998.  The split system is in good condition.  Temperature control is managed throughout the building by a pneumatic system consisting of one central air compressor which supplies compressed air to thermostats, regulators, and damper controls on each floor.  It’s estimated the temperature controls were installed around 1993.  This type of temperature control system is outdated.  It is recommended the temperature control system be replaced with a modern digital control system in the next 5 years.
desc_mechanical: Life Safety:Fire protection specialties are present.  System components include: hard wired smoke and CO2 detectors, pull stations, automated fire suppression, monitored fire alarms, standpipes and wet sprinklers. The standpipe system is provided throughout the building and the sprinkler system is provided for the basement.  With the exception of the piping, major components of the standpipe and sprinkler system, such as the main control valve, standpipe valves, and sprinkler heads were replaced around 2011.  The fire protection system is in good condition.  It appears the fire alarm system was replaced around 2011.  The system is a modern fully addressable and centrally monitored system.   Pull stations and audio visual alarms are present and located as required.  The fire alarm system is in good condition.
desc_life_safety: Other Electrical:No emergency power system is provided to the building.
desc_electrical: Accessibility:An abbreviated accessibility survey was scheduled for this facility.  In general, the facility does not contain the required features to be considered to be accessible for persons with disabilities. In order to provide access, numerous upgrades would be required including replacement of the elevator, installation of wheelchair accessible restrooms, installation of code compliant handrails on exterior steps, installation of accessible signage, modifications to the reception desk, and replacement of non-compliant door hardware.  This project survey reviewed selected accessibility features.
